claims.text: Adding 0.5–2 wt% graphene nanoplatelets to a W–Cu composite will increase its thermal conductivity.
Adding graphene nanoplatelets will allow the W–Cu composite to retain mechanical durability.
Adding graphene nanoplatelets will allow the W–Cu composite to retain irradiation resistance.
The intended graphene-nanoplatelet fraction is 0.5–2 wt%.
The proposed composite is intended to operate at temperatures up to 1000°C.
The proposed composite is intended to operate under neutron irradiation associated with fusion-reactor joints.
Graphene nanoplatelets will be dispersed within the W–Cu matrix.
Graphene nanoplatelets have high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will act as thermal bridges between W and Cu phases.
Graphene nanoplatelets will reduce interfacial thermal resistance between W and Cu phases.
The layered structure of graphene nanoplatelets will mechanically reinforce the W–Cu composite.
Graphene nanoplatelets will mitigate defect propagation and thereby improve or preserve irradiation resistance.
The modified composite will have 10–20% higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable W–Cu composite without graphene nanoplatelets.
The modified composite will have mechanical durability comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
The modified composite will have irradiation resistance comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
Agglomeration of graphene nanoplatelets may degrade mechanical properties or thermal conductivity.
Adding graphene nanoplatelets above an optimal fraction may degrade mechanical properties or thermal conductivity.
